provenance.note: Jaspers & Dautzenberg (2002) constants as stated by Burns et al. 2012 Eq. (1.2), with Tr = 20 C and Tf = 1490 C; also used by xiu-2019-1045-grinding-fe Table 4. Burns et al. report that FE simulations with this set under-predict the peak tool-chip temperature by hundreds of C and that rapidly heated 1045 is stiffer below the eutectoid (723 C). Alternative: Murugesan & Jung 2019 (Materials 12:609) fitted A 50.1, B 176.1 for hot forming at 1223 K reference, not suitable for cutting. The Jaspers & Dautzenberg original (J. Mater. Process. Technol., 2002) could not be read in the second research round either (paywalled; no open thesis copy found), so the set is confirmed only through Burns et al. and xiu-2019-1045-grinding-fe.
20 C; Table 1 gives 7850 (20 C) falling to 7649 (1000 C)
taken from the 0.25-0.30 ratio found for 304 stainless (zou-2026-304-min-cutting-thickness); no 1045-specific value read

0.78 = Albrecht-method estimate from the ETH force data (klippel-2022 Sect. 3.4), which the authors call very high and likely inaccurate because of BUE and segmentation; 0.3-0.6 is the range of Coulomb coefficients used in the FE studies read for other steels; 0.5 chosen
